title: What If an Ice Shelf Vanished in 35 Days? Larsen B Did

scenes.text: What if a slab of Antarctic ice bigger than Rhode Island vanished in a month? One did.
In January 2002, the Larsen B ice shelf began to shatter. Satellites watched it break apart.
It covered about 3,250 square kilometers, and it took just 35 days to fall away completely.
The ice was floating, but it had been holding something back: the glaciers behind it.
Without that brake, the glaciers behind it sped up by about 300 percent on average.
Their ice loss jumped from 2 to 4 billion tons a year to 22 to 40. The shelf was a cork.

description:
What if an Antarctic ice shelf vanished in about a month?
In 2002 the Larsen B shelf, around 3,250 square kilometers, broke up in 35 days, and the glaciers behind it sped up by roughly 300 percent.
